title: Prime-field small-x factor bases: relation yield and cost (B11/A5)
question: Prime-field factor-base question (B11/A5 open requirement): for E/F_p (p prime) and the factor base V_B = {Q in E(F_p): x(Q) < B} with B = p^{1/m}, the probability that a uniformly random R in E(F_p) is a sum of m points of V_B is about |V_B|^m/(m! p) (heuristic), and finding such decompositions via Semaev summation polynomials (S_3 for m=2) costs at least as much as rho at toy sizes; no choice of (m, B) yields a relation-collection cost below sqrt(p) group operations on prime fields at toy sizes.
rationale: Highest-significance open direction for universal ECDLP identified independently by agents A (A5) and B (B11); cheap falsification at toy sizes.
claims: Prime-field factor-base question (B11/A5 open requirement): for E/F_p (p prime) and the factor base V_B = {Q in E(F_p): x(Q) < B} with B = p^{1/m}, the probability that a uniformly random R in E(F_p) is a sum of m points of V_B is about |V_B|^m/(m! p) (heuristic), and finding such decompositions via Semaev summation polynomials (S_3 for m=2) costs at least as much as rho at toy sizes; no choice of (m, B) yields a relation-collection cost below sqrt(p) group operations on prime fields at toy sizes.
next_action: Prime-field index calculus via summation polynomials looks closed at toy sizes for m <= 3 with these bases (both relation finding and linear algebra). Remaining logically open route: a factor base where decomposition is found by a non-elimination method (e.g. lattice / small-root) — record as speculative; deprioritize.
notes: Registered by PI. Known context (unverified recollection by agents): Semaev 2004; Petit-Kosters-Messeng PKC 2016; Diem; prime-field variants remain exponential. | ECDLP-12 (pre-registered, PI-reproduced): SURVIVES on tested domain (12 prime-order curves near 2^12..2^18, m in {2,3}, beta in {0.5,1,2}, exact enumeration). Best total cost 15.7 x sqrt(p) at 2^18 (falsification needed < 0.5 x). Measured pi tracks n^m/(m! r) within 0-30% (n counts signed points); the (2n)^m form in the statement double counts signs (statement imprecise). Semaev S_3 route verified (8000 group-law checks; 600/600 vs brute force) and ~2-2.7x cheaper than naive scanning but not cheaper than a full (m-1)-sum table (BSGS-like). Fitted exponents 0.6-1.0; agent derived m/(2m-1) > 1/2 inside its table cost model (not general). End-to-end toy index calculus recovered k correctly at p=4001, 15791 (40-52 x sqrt(p)). Toy sizes; 4-point exponent fits; unit costs. | ECDLP-13 (PI-reproduced): Literature: Petit–Kosters–Messeng PKC 2016 (full PDF read by agent) already proposes prime-field factor bases from x in a coset of a smooth-order multiplicative subgroup and from isogeny cosets; their complexity is stated as open (Groebner experiments only); beating sqrt(p) needs system-solving cost T < p^{1/2-1/m}. Toy test (24 curves, 2^12..2^18, m=2): F1 cosets, x=t^2, x=1/t and small-x all match random sets of equal size in coverage and additive energy within ~1%; no faster-than-|V| decomposition finding found (Semaev S_3 scan ~34|V| field mults per R). Structured factor bases give no advantage at m=2 on the tested domain. Novelty note: the agent's F1 proposal duplicates PKM 2016 (recorded, not claimed). | ECDLP-16 (pre-registered, PI-reproduced verify/k16/e2e; only timing fields differ): m=3, |V| ~ p^{1/3}, p from 4129 to ~2^20 (4 curves per bucket; 2 at 2^20). S_3/S_4 verified (2400 tuples each; root sets exact on 300 triples, 0 spurious on 2098 controls). Best method M1 (pair-sum table) per-relation T = 54-320 counted mults vs p^{1/6} = 4-10; fitted T-exponent 0.22-0.30 (crude, 4-5 points) — threshold T < p^{1/6} NOT achieved; total 44-83 sqrt(p), exponent ~0.61. M2 (S_4 resultant/root test) 300-800x costlier; M3 elimination analytic: degrees Theta(h)..Theta(h^2) so root/gcd stages cost at least that. Small-x, PKM-coset and random bases indistinguishable. Linear algebra model 3|V|^2 = 3p^{2/3} alone exceeds sqrt(p) for |V| = p^{1/3} (model, not measurement). End-to-end toy index calculus correct (p=4129). Agent corrected a PI task-note complexity statement (X^h mod q costs O(deg^2 log h)).
